headline: GxE-aware genomic prediction and sparse testing designs in Miscanthus breeding
label: Genomic Prediction In Miscanthus
summary: Sparse multi-environment testing could cut Miscanthus phenotyping costs about fivefold, so predictive accuracy under reduced trialing now matters.
synthesis: The three preprints treat genomic prediction in Miscanthus breeding populations, with genotype-by-environment (GxE) interaction as the dominant modeling variable. One study reports that cross-validation schemes and GxE-aware models raise predictive ability for biomass yield over main-effect models. A second evaluates genomic prediction under sparse testing designs in multi-environment trials, finding that the GxE model performs best and that phenotyping costs could be cut about fivefold. A third benchmarks five genomic prediction models, including multi-trait multi-environment approaches, on 336 Miscanthus sacchariflorus genotypes under three cross-validation schemes. The shared thread is the joint treatment of environmental structure and trial design. The question is shifting from which genomic model predicts best toward how sparsely phenotypes can be collected while maintaining predictive accuracy.
